title: Protocol for efficient fluorescence 3′ end-labeling of native noncoding RNA domains
author: Awwad, Rahmouni, et al.
materials: RNA purification and recovery was performed under native-like conditions maintaining the samples at room temperature at all time, as previously described [4,13]. Throughout the protocol, recovery and purification of RNA are performed using centrifugal filtration (see following sections), such as the commercially-available AmiconⓇ Ultra Centrifugal Filters (Millipore). The AmiconⓇ filters are commonly utilized for the concentration and desalting of protein samples prior to various chromatography applications, such as HPLC, and they are ideal for removal of solutes, nucleotides, primers and other low molecular weight components from reactions. This step allows for buffer exchange as well as filtering out unreacted NTPs, digested proteins and DNA fragments as well as short abortive transcripts from our RNA preparations.

Following transcription, the reactions were supplemented with 1.2 mM CaCl2 and DNase I (2000 U/ml; New England BioLabs) and incubated for 30 min at 37 °C, and subsequently with proteinase K (20 mg/ml; Thermo Scientific) and incubated for 45 min at 37 °C. Immediately afterwards, reactions were diluted with a HEPES-based filtration buffer (HEPES-FB; 100 mM NH4Ac, 8 mM HEPES pH=7.3, 0.1 mM Na-EDTA pH=8.5) and applied to Amicon Ultra-4 centrifugal filters (Millipore; 30 kDa molecular weight cut-off). Centrifugation was done at 4000 g for 15 min at room temperature. Following filtration, Nanodrop measurements were taken to ensure sample purity and homogeneity as well as sufficient elimination of enzymes and other proteins as represented by an A260/A280 nm absorbance ratio that ranges between 2.0 and 2.5.

steps.title: Maintain native conditions
steps.instruction: Keep all RNA samples at room temperature throughout the procedure and avoid salt‑ethanol precipitation, freezing, or extreme agitation to preserve secondary structure.

steps.title: Digest nucleic acid contaminants
steps.instruction: After transcription, add 1.2 mM CaCl₂ and DNase I (2000 U ml⁻¹, NEB) to the reaction and incubate 30 min at 37 °C; then add proteinase K (20 mg ml⁻¹, Thermo Scientific) and incubate 45 min at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.2 mM CaCl₂ to the transcription mixture.
Add DNase I to a final concentration of 2000 U ml⁻¹.
Add proteinase K to a final concentration of 20 mg ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Dilute and filter RNA
steps.instruction: Dilute the reaction with HEPES‑based filtration buffer (HEPES‑FB: 100 mM NH₄Ac, 8 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 0.1 mM Na‑EDTA pH 8.5) and apply to an Amicon Ultra‑4 centrifugal filter (30 kDa MWCO); centrifuge at 4000 g for 15 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Prepare HEPES‑FB containing 100 mM NH₄Ac, 8 mM HEPES (pH 7.3), 0.1 mM Na‑EDTA (pH 8.5).
Dilute the digested reaction with the HEPES‑FB buffer.
Load the diluted mixture onto an Amicon Ultra‑4 filter (30 kDa).
Centrifuge at 4000 g for 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure RNA purity
steps.instruction: Take a Nanodrop reading of the filtrate and verify that the A260/A280 ratio is between 2.0 and 2.5, indicating pure RNA.

steps.title: Check homogeneity on native gel
steps.instruction: Run an aliquot of the purified RNA on a native polyacrylamide or native agarose gel, stain with ethidium bromide, and visualize to confirm a single, well‑defined band.

steps.title: Perform SEC quality control
steps.instruction: Optional: assess RNA homogeneity by size‑exclusion chromatography using a Tricorn column packed with Sephacryl S300; wash the column with 4 column volumes (CV) of DEPC‑treated water, equilibrate with 4 CV of HEPES‑FB, then run the sample at room temperature with HEPES‑FB as the running buffer, monitoring UV absorbance.

substeps.instruction: Wash Tricorn column (Sephacryl S300) with 4 CV DEPC‑treated water.
Equilibrate column with 4 CV HEPES‑FB buffer.
Load purified RNA onto the column.
Run chromatography at room temperature using HEPES‑FB as the mobile phase.
Collect UV absorbance data to verify a single sharp peak.
